text.p: An earthquake measuring 5.2 on the Richter scale was struck off Nicaragua's Pacific coast on Sunday, Nicaragua's Institute of Territorial Studies said.

The quake, which sent a slight tremor through the Nicaraguan capital in the afternoon, had its epicentre under the Pacific Ocean 142 miles (230 kms) south of Managua off the Costa Rican coast, the institute reported.
There were no injuries or damages reported.
A major earthquake in the same area but closer to shore in 1992 generated a giant sea wave, or tsunami, that killed more than 100 Nicaraguans.
The capital of Managua has been destroyed by earthquakes twice this century, in 1931 and 1972.
